# Experiments

this chapter aims to evaluate the effectiveness of pysealer and its defense in depth capabilities. the experiments introduced in this chapter are designed to assess the tool's security. 
- pysealer used to defend against mcp tool poisoning (figure 2) and shadowing attacks(figure 3) that i introduced in the introduction
- comparing the security features of pysealer compared to mcp scan, the one of the most popular mcp security tools on the market. (reference mcp scan here.)
- highlighting pysealers internal test suite that measures the effectiveness of the decorator insertion and signature verification process

## Experimental Design

descrive how it is difficult to evaluate security related tools. should sound human. security tools are tough to evaluate because of the nature of security. you can't just run a test and see if it works, you have to simulate attacks and see if it can defend against them. for this reason, the experiments in this chapter are designed to simulate what a real-world mcp tool poisoning and tool shadowing attack could look like and evaluate pysealer's performance in defending against them. 

this chapter contains 4 primary experiments. 
- pysealer tool poisoining
- pysealer tool shadowing
- mcp scan tool poisoning
- mcp scan tool shadowing
(reference experiments repo here)

the experiments are all run within on script (run_experiments.py) that simulates the attacks and shows each tools output.this script does x.another important concept when performing computational experiments is reproduciblity. for these experiments. docker. python version. pysealer version. mcp scan version. all are important to control.

one last things that is important to note is the xethics of performing security related experiments. running these experiments on real mcp servers could cause harm to real systems and data. for this reason, all experiments in this chapter are conducted in a controlled environment using simulated attacks. its also important to note that

## Internal Test Suite

AND internal test suite measuring effectiveness of decorator insertion (can do multiple experiments just have them relate to security) pytest cite
Decorator insertion accuracy: Percentage of functions/classes successfully decorated across diverse codebases
Signature verification accuracy: False positive/negative rates when detecting unauthorized modifications
Performance overhead: Time impact of lock/check operations on codebases of varying sizes (10, 100, 1000+ functions)
